svg.text: Sovereign MCP Platform · Solution Design — one agent, two MCP servers, one local model, nothing leaves the machine

Answer from a local corpus with citations, reach for OCR only when the index cannot see the file, refuse to answer when the corpus does not support it — on ONE workstation, fully offline, with zero writes to C:\.
① QUERY PATH — question → discover capabilities → search the index → parse what the index cannot see → grounded answer
The agent decides; the servers declare. Routing is driven entirely by what each server advertises at connect time — adding a third server needs no change to the reasoning loop.
the user never names a tool
routing is the agent's job, not theirs
below it: reported as no match
prebuilt ReAct loop · capped at 6 tool rounds
and, where useful, the chunk id
the test asserts none was invented
The disclosure that makes multi-server routing work
The index and the corpus are not the same set. search_documents reports files it has no chunks for.
Without that line the agent abstained on a question whose answer sat in an un-ingested scanned PDF.
rag_server knows this from its own index and its own corpus directory — it never learns that docs_server exists.
Prompts are server-scoped; orchestration is not
rag_answer tells the model to abstain when search finds nothing — right alone, wrong once a parser exists.
Cross-server guidance is composed by the host, from its live routing table. Neither server is modified.
It rides in the user message: a 4B model follows the closing numbered instruction over anything in the system prompt.
② MCP SURFACE — what each server exposes, and which side of the protocol owns it
All three primitives are exercised end to end. Tools and prompts belong to the servers; resources are host-controlled, so the host has to bridge them.
ChromaDB, file-based · embeddings baked into the image
so the running container never reaches the network
chunking and IDs shared with the ingest script — they cannot drift
containerised of necessity: Tesseract on Windows
filenames are untrusted input — path traversal is refused
PRIMITIVE OWNERSHIP — who decides what, and why it matters
Schema passes through untouched; adding a tool needs no host change
Fetched via prompts/get, never hardcoded in the host
Not model-addressable, so chunk:// is re-exposed as a tool
stdio — no socket at all. Stronger posture: no port to
firewall, no key to rotate, no session to hijack.
Selected by a flag, not a fork of the server: transport
and authorisation are separable from capability.
stdio cannot cross a container boundary — it needs a
parent owning the child's stdio, and siblings share none.
So the Phase 5 auth work turned out to be a prerequisite, not a demo.

pdfminer extracts zero characters from the OCR fixture · a paraphrase sharing no keywords retrieves the right passage at 0.718 · a keyless POST inside the compose network returns 401 · zero huggingface requests at runtime · docker volume ls is empty
③ RUNTIME & DEPLOYMENT — where every byte actually lives, and how the model is reached
Docker Engine runs inside a custom-imported WSL2 distro, not Docker Desktop, so the data-root sits on M:\ by construction rather than by configuration that could drift.
ext4.vhdx imported onto M:\ · compose network only, no published ports
server URLs set → HTTP; unset → stdio
the reasoning loop never learns which
so no request pays for load
lazy loading had made a build-time
no top-level volumes: block, so nothing
lands in Docker's internal volume store
every byte stays visible on M:\
it resolves to the distro itself
is never exposed to the LAN
no Ollama, no vLLM, no second
LLM_ENDPOINT=http://host.docker.internal:8001/v1 — every reasoning call, from every service
④ GOVERNANCE — the four constraints this build is actually judged against, and how each is enforced rather than intended
Enforced by construction, not by policy: the distro's
vhdx is imported onto M:\, so the Docker data-root
uv cache, Python installs, HF cache and TEMP are all
~1 KB, a hard WSL2 requirement with no override.
One GPU, one model, one endpoint. Every service in
the stack points at port 8001 or it is out of policy.
Embeddings run on CPU via ONNX rather than being
given a GPU server of their own.
Verified as one process, not one socket — the port
proxy legitimately adds a second listener that loads
no model and consumes no VRAM.
Checked before any MCP handler runs, with
Fails closed: with the key unset the server refuses to
Deliberately NOT provided: per-user identity, per-tool
scoping, rotation, audit trail, TLS, rate limiting.
ChromaDB telemetry is disabled and LangSmith
tracing is switched off before LangChain is even
imported — both ship on by default.
Embedding weights are baked in at build time, not
Lazy initialisation quietly turns a build-time
dependency into a runtime one. In an air-gapped
design that is a correctness bug, not a slow start.
Open discrepancies — recorded, not quietly patched
HLD §2 draws stdio between sibling containers, which is not realisable · HLD §3 calls HTTP a "Phase 5 variant" when it is now the compose default

policy §2 budgets rag_server at 500–700 MB against an actual 933 MB — the largest single contributor is an 83 MB Kubernetes client that chromadb pulls in for a distributed mode this file-based store never uses
